text: Caldwell Precision Manufacturing just licensed ServiceNow after years of running support out of a shared mailbox and a spreadsheet. You're the implementation consultant. This capstone is the kickoff meeting, the checklist it produces, and then four lessons of real configuration against that checklist.

Five stakeholders, five real asks, each pulled almost word for word from the actual kickoff notes. The VP of Operations wants Meridian, the production ERP running work orders and shipping across all three plants, back in under an hour when it goes down. The plant IT manager is tired of reopening the same ticket for the Line 3 label printer instead of actually fixing it. The CFO wants nobody touching Meridian's production configuration without approval and a documented record of exactly what changed. HR wants new-hire laptop and software access handled as a catalog item instead of three separate emails and a phone call. And the service desk supervisor wants a knowledge base so agents stop answering the same password-reset and VPN question fifteen times a day.

Translate those five asks into a real checklist. Faster Priority 1 resolution and the recurring Line 3 ticket both route through Incident and Problem Management, built in Lesson 30, alongside a risk-based Change path for Meridian specifically. Provable SLA commitments, the self-service onboarding catalog, a searchable knowledge base, and a self-service portal widget all get built in Lesson 31.

Notice these are two different problems, not one. Fixing Meridian faster is Incident Management's job: restore service fast, even with a temporary workaround. Fixing the Line 3 printer for good is Problem Management's job: find the permanent cause, deliberately slower, by design. And because Meridian is the one system that can stop shipments company-wide, it earns its own risk-based Change path instead of the same generic approval as everything else.

That's the full requirements checklist this capstone builds against. Next, Lesson 30 turns the Incident, Problem, and Change rows into real configuration, each one tied back to a specific stakeholder ask from this meeting.
